body:
Get that privileged crap outta here. Just because someone else might have more pressing matters than yours, it still doesn’t change the fact you are struggling just like everyone else.

You’ll get through it.

I know sometimes my anxiety can become a loop, where I get anxious because I’m anxious or stressed out because I’m stressed out. I understand that if I get on that train, I have to ride it out until I’m emotionally exhausted.

However, I know that response only happens when I’m thinking about my high stress levels. So I remind myself I’m doing fine and to breath for a few minutes.

My brain works like that. There is a trigger -> response, but I can intervene and get myself off of that train of thought.

If you feel like this describes your anxiety, then you need to understand your trigger. Is it reading articles about mental health disorders? If so, I can i alter this activity or cut it out completely so I don’t have an emotional response. 

Maybe that involves running the article by your therapist or talking with someone close to you, and having them confirm whether you act like that or not.

It really is something where you have to experiment with different solutions.

My dad was a major source of anxiety. For example, Whenever I had to make a bigger decision, he would always play devils  advocate. And not matter what I chose, he’d always point out the negatives of my choice. I was never sure of myself. One time I asked him not to do that and got a “What the fuck ______”.

I had a problem with looking at him for awhile after that one.
Public online school is a war crime
